candidates.name: Cerebral vasculitis
support_spans: Noncontrast head CT demonstrated a hypodense area in the right basal ganglia with mass effect but no hemorrhage

Brain MRI revealed T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in the right basal ganglia and internal capsule with mild surrounding edema, scattered small foci of restricted diffusion, and subtle punctate blooming on susceptibility-weighted images
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings are consistent with cerebral vasculitis, which is an inflammation of the blood vessels in the brain.

candidates.name: Pyogenic brain abscess
support_spans: Lumbar puncture yielded an opening pressure of 23 cm H₂O and slightly hazy cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) with 538 WBCs/mm³
Repeat lumbar puncture showed an opening pressure of 30 cm H₂O, 1762 WBCs/mm³
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms and CSF findings are consistent with a pyogenic brain abscess, which is a collection of pus in the brain tissue.

candidates.name: Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy
support_spans: Brain MRI revealed T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in the right basal ganglia and internal capsule with mild surrounding edema, scattered small foci of restricted diffusion, and subtle punctate blooming on susceptibility-weighted images
Repeat MRI demonstrated progression with new involvement of the left basal ganglia, increased diffusion restriction, development of necrosis, and new peripheral contrast enhancement
contradict_spans: John Cunningham virus PCR was negative
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings are consistent with progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy, which is a rare and often fatal viral disease caused by the JC virus.
